result.label: Source-read

claims.claim: Section 337(a) sets a four-year period for an action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing.
claims.quote:
Within four years:
(a) An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing, except as provided in Section 336a;
claims.note: The four-year heading applies to subdivision (a).

claims.claim: The four-year rule is subject to the Section 336a exception.
claims.note: The separate proviso concerning real-property security is outside the stated unsecured-contract scope.

claims.claim: Section 337 does not state when the four-year period starts for an ordinary written-contract claim.
claims.quote:
Within four years:
(a) An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing, except as provided in Section 336a;
claims.note: Subdivision (a) gives the duration but no starting event for the scoped claim. The starting events in (b) and (c) concern account-stated and rescission claims, respectively.

claims.claim: The saved sources contain no other rule on when that period starts for an ordinary written-contract claim.
claims.quote: The period in which an action may be commenced under this section shall only be extended pursuant to Section 360.
claims.note: CCP-337 is the only saved text. Its reference to Section 360 concerns extension, not the initial starting event.

result.summary: The saved text gives the period and the stated exception, but no starting event for the ordinary unsecured written-contract claim described in the draft.
